experiments.name: Water balance: global precipitation = global evaporation
experiments.physics: Over decades the atmosphere stores no extra water, so what evaporates must fall.
experiments.source: Bosilovich, Robertson, Takacs et al. (2017), J. Climate 30, 1177–1196

experiments.name: Clausius-Clapeyron: ocean humidity vs temperature
experiments.physics: Saturation vapour pressure grows ~7 % per K; with near-constant relative humidity, so does q.

experiments.name: Arctic amplification
experiments.physics: Sea-ice and snow loss lower the surface albedo, so the Arctic warms faster than the globe.
experiments.expected: Arctic (≥ 66.5°N) trend / global trend between 2 and 5
experiments.source: Rantanen et al. (2022), Communications Earth & Environment 3, 168

experiments.name: Mount Pinatubo eruption (June 1991)
experiments.physics: Stratospheric sulfate aerosol reflects sunlight: aerosol optical depth peaks, the surface cools the next year.
experiments.expected: global AOD maximum in 1991 or 1992 AND 1992 global T2M ≥ 0.1 °C below the 1990–91 mean
experiments.source: Hansen et al. (1992), GRL 19, 215–218; Soden et al. (2002), Science 296, 727–730

experiments.name: El Niño events in the tropical Pacific
experiments.physics: El Niño warms the central/east equatorial Pacific; the data must show the documented events.
experiments.expected: ≥ 2 of the 3 warmest Niño-3.4 DJF anomalies are 1982–83, 1997–98, 2015–16
experiments.source: NOAA CPC Oceanic Niño Index (ONI) event list

experiments.name: Snow amount vs temperature (NH land 40–70°N)
experiments.physics: Warmer years melt more snow and turn more snowfall into rain.
experiments.expected: correlation of annual snow and temperature anomalies < −0.3
